newsitem.title: UK: Japanese stocks in London led up by blue chips.
newsitem.headline: Japanese stocks in London led up by blue chips.

text.p: Japanese shares in London made firm progress on Thursday with blue chip stocks well bid on the back of the yen's slide against the dollar, traders said.
By 1540 the Nikkei 50 index was trading at 1,349.52 points, up 7.74 points or 0.58 percent after an overnight fall in Tokyo. The Nikkei closed at 17,909.46, down 104.42.

As the yen slipped to a new 47-month low of 119.69 against the dollar, investors in London put their money into blue chip exporters, traders said. Fujitsu was the main gainer, at 1,182.5 yen, up 32.5 from the Tokyo close, after Nomura upgraded its recommendation on the stock to "buy" from "hold".
Traders said other blue chips rose in the wake of Fujitsu's gains, although banking stocks were quiet.
On the technical front, one trader said a "pennant" pattern was forming in the Nikkei 250 which could break sometime over the next month.
"If we break on the upside, it could go to 18,500 or maybe 19,000. On the downside, it could break but we think there is support at 17,300," the trader said.
